findings.title: {%endcomment%}/{%endverbatim%} without inner whitespace no longer close blocks
findings.explanation: `_comment_end_re` and `_verbatim_end_re` need `[^\S\n]+` (at least one space or tab) after `{%`. The old code compared stripped content (`content == 'endverbatim'`, and the parser's `skip_past('endcomment')`), so `{%endverbatim%}` and `{%endcomment%}` used to close their blocks. In `_tag_re_split` the raw regex now never matches these forms. The remaining template is emitted as one TEXT token, and the parser raises 'Unclosed tag comment/verbatim'. This happens on every DebugLexer run, and in Lexer whenever the template has any `{% comment`/`{% verbatim` opening (for example `{% comment %}a{%endcomment%}`). The named-verbatim regex uses `*`, so the three end regexes are also inconsistent with each other.
findings.suggestion: Use `[^\S\n]*` after BLOCK_TAG_START in both `_comment_end_re` and `_verbatim_end_re`, so they match whatever `token_string[2:-2].strip()` accepted before.

findings.title: Fast-path check misses {%verbatim%}, so Lexer and DebugLexer diverge
findings.explanation: `_raw_start_re` needs `\s+` between `{%` and `verbatim`/`comment`. `_raw_end_tag_re` strips the content, so it treats `{%verbatim%}` as a raw opener. The verbatim handling that used to sit in `create_token` has been removed. For `{%verbatim%}{{ x }}{% if y %}{%endverbatim%}`, `Lexer.tokenize()` therefore takes the plain `tag_re.split` path. The block body is lexed as VAR/BLOCK tokens, so `{{ x }}` renders as '' through `VerbatimNode(nodelist.render(Context()))`, and inner block tags are compiled and executed. Before this change the body came out literally. `DebugLexer` always uses `_tag_re_split`: it treats the block as raw, then cannot find `{%endverbatim%}` (previous finding) and raises. The same template now gives different results with debug on and off, and both differ from the old behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Make `_raw_start_re` accept optional whitespace (`%s\s*(?:comment|verbatim)\b`), so its false negatives are a superset of what `_raw_end_tag_re` recognises. Better, build both from the same normalisation, and add tests for the no-space forms with debug on and off.

findings.title: Token-type dict rebuilt on every tag token in hot lexer path
findings.explanation: `create_token` builds a new three-entry dict for every tag token. Tokenizing is a hot path when templates compile, and the old code used plain comparisons. This adds an allocation and a hash lookup for every tag in every template.
findings.suggestion: Hoist the mapping to a module- or class-level constant (e.g. `_TOKEN_TYPE_BY_START = {...}`) and look it up there.

findings.title: Closing-tag regex requires whitespace; {%endcomment%} no longer closes
findings.explanation: The comment and verbatim closing regexes need at least one whitespace character after `{%`. The old lexer stripped the tag content, so `{%endverbatim%}` and `{%endcomment%}` closed the block. In the raw-aware path, those forms are no longer found. The verbatim or comment block then stays open to the end of the template. This only affects unusual spacing. The named-verbatim regex uses `*`, so it's inconsistent with these two.
findings.suggestion: Use `[^\S\n]*` instead of `[^\S\n]+` before endcomment and endverbatim.
